gaps.criterion_why: The leaf itself promises the fire never floods most of the map within a few days, and a player would notice a fire that swallows the map; the fix asks for a share read judged against a wind-off control, a relative check that a correct mod can pass without pinning any tuning number.
gaps.judge_criterion_why: The leaf's own words name the flood as the thing it must not read as, and the contract requires a control that rules out that plausible alternative.
gaps.observed: The leaf's bar is 'never most of the map inside a few days' (tree.json:31). The scene watches 'for a game day', capturing 'the front and its black trail at play zoom' (scenes.json:15). Its measured expect is 'burning ground whose centre moves, a growing scorched trail' (scenes.json:16), and a flood also burns and also moves its centre. The judge who must confirm 'not a flood over the whole map' is shown captures of the front only; the chain behind them (validation.py::_r6_burn_line, front_walks) crops each capture to at most 30 cells around the fire. The control rules out only 'a vanilla wildfire incident or a test-lit fire passing for the burn line' (scenes.json:20). No reading of how much of the map has burned exists, and no control shows that the instrument can see a flood.
gaps.since: tree.json leaf burn_line_walks: the experience now says 'must not read as a flood that takes the whole map and its grass' and the oracle adds 'never most of the map inside a few days'. scenes.json sc_burn_line_walks: the expect changed from 'one contiguous line' to 'a natural grass fire ... not a flood over the whole map'.

gaps.what: burn_line_walks now promises a fire that is never a flood over the map ('never most of the map inside a few days'). The live scene measures nothing that could tell the burn line apart from a flood.
gaps.would_pass: sc_burn_line_walks, or a sibling acceptance scene, reads the burned share of open plantable ground over the map (a burn-history or scar census) at the end of each day for the 'few days' window. It expects the share to stay well short of most of the map. A same-seed control with windCarriesFireEnabled off (vanilla's even spread) must read a clearly larger share, so the instrument is shown to see a flood. Both readings are relative, so no tuning number becomes the bar.

gaps.criterion_why: Fire that follows the wind is something a player sees, and testing one bearing with no check that the wind was actually set cannot tell a fire that follows the wind from one hard-coded to run one way; a reversed-bearing run and an asserted start are fair and attainable.
gaps.judge_criterion_why: 'Whatever the wind' is a claim across wind bearings, and the contract asks for an asserted start.
gaps.observed: The leaf says 'It must not read as a fire that spreads the same way whatever the wind' (tree.json:67). The start reads 'the wind set across them' (scenes.json:39): one wind, not asserted, whereas the scene's own wording asserts other starts. Its entry point wind_burn_live.py sets one bearing (90) and its verdict rows do not check the bearing returned or the probe's carries flag. The mod's burn path reads the map's wind bearing, and an offline fuzz covers all bearings, so a fixed-direction build is unlikely. That is why this gap is polish.
